falseSynonyms.zh: surprising = unexpected amazing = often stronger; may combine surprise with admiration or wonder Compare: - It was surprising that he arrived early. - His recovery was amazing. Something can be surprising without being impressive.
falseSynonyms.point: surprising = unexpected amazing = often stronger; may combine surprise with admiration or wonder Compare: - It was surprising that he arrived early. - His recovery was amazing. Something can be surprising without being impressive.

falseSynonyms.zh: impressive = deserving admiration amazing = may involve surprise, wonder, or strong praise Compare: - Her technical knowledge is impressive. - Her sudden recovery was amazing. An expected high-quality performance can be impressive without being surprising.
falseSynonyms.point: impressive = deserving admiration amazing = may involve surprise, wonder, or strong praise Compare: - Her technical knowledge is impressive. - Her sudden recovery was amazing. An expected high-quality performance can be impressive without being surprising.

falseSynonyms.zh: beautiful specifically describes beauty. amazing is broader. Compare: - a beautiful garden - an amazing discovery A discovery can be amazing without being beautiful.
falseSynonyms.point: beautiful specifically describes beauty. amazing is broader. Compare: - a beautiful garden - an amazing discovery A discovery can be amazing without being beautiful.

falseSynonyms.zh: interesting = holding attention or curiosity amazing = causing strong surprise, admiration, or wonder Compare: - an interesting article - an amazing achievement Interesting does not automatically mean extraordinary.
falseSynonyms.point: interesting = holding attention or curiosity amazing = causing strong surprise, admiration, or wonder Compare: - an interesting article - an amazing achievement Interesting does not automatically mean extraordinary.

falseSynonyms.zh: shocking often has a negative meaning: causing horror, outrage, or severe surprise. Compare: - amazing news = often very good - shocking news = often disturbing or bad Do not automatically replace positive amazing with shocking.
falseSynonyms.point: shocking often has a negative meaning: causing horror, outrage, or severe surprise. Compare: - amazing news = often very good - shocking news = often disturbing or bad Do not automatically replace positive amazing with shocking.

falseSynonyms.zh: Both can mean “hard to believe.” But in everyday praise: - incredible often sounds clearly positive - unbelievable can be positive, negative, or genuinely doubtful Examples: - an incredible performance - unbelievable incompetence - an unbelievable story Context matters.
falseSynonyms.point: Both can mean “hard to believe.” But in everyday praise: - incredible often sounds clearly positive - unbelievable can be positive, negative, or genuinely doubtful Examples: - an incredible performance - unbelievable incompetence - an unbelievable story Context matters.

falseSynonyms.zh: spectacular = dramatic, visually impressive, striking wonderful = very good, enjoyable, delightful Compare: - spectacular fireworks - a wonderful friend “Spectacular friend” is usually unnatural unless describing something unusually dramatic about the person.
falseSynonyms.point: spectacular = dramatic, visually impressive, striking wonderful = very good, enjoyable, delightful Compare: - spectacular fireworks - a wonderful friend “Spectacular friend” is usually unnatural unless describing something unusually dramatic about the person.

falseSynonyms.zh: stunning often emphasizes beauty or immediate visual impact. astonishing emphasizes surprise. Compare: - a stunning dress - an astonishing discovery
falseSynonyms.point: stunning often emphasizes beauty or immediate visual impact. astonishing emphasizes surprise. Compare: - a stunning dress - an astonishing discovery

falseSynonyms.zh: remarkable = noteworthy, unusual exceptional = far above the normal standard Compare: - remarkable progress - exceptional service There is overlap, but the emphasis differs.
falseSynonyms.point: remarkable = noteworthy, unusual exceptional = far above the normal standard Compare: - remarkable progress - exceptional service There is overlap, but the emphasis differs.

falseSynonyms.zh: Modern informal awesome often simply means “excellent.” awe-inspiring retains the stronger literal meaning of producing awe. Compare: - That pizza was awesome. - The scale of the universe is awe-inspiring.
falseSynonyms.point: Modern informal awesome often simply means “excellent.” awe-inspiring retains the stronger literal meaning of producing awe. Compare: - That pizza was awesome. - The scale of the universe is awe-inspiring.

falseSynonyms.zh: phenomenal = adjective phenomenon = noun Correct: - phenomenal growth - a remarkable phenomenon Incorrect: - phenomenon growth ✗
falseSynonyms.point: phenomenal = adjective phenomenon = noun Correct: - phenomenal growth - a remarkable phenomenon Incorrect: - phenomenon growth ✗

falseSynonyms.zh: wonderful = extremely good miraculous = so unlikely that it seems like a miracle Compare: - a wonderful holiday - a miraculous escape Do not call an ordinary pleasant experience “miraculous” unless deliberately exaggerating.
falseSynonyms.point: wonderful = extremely good miraculous = so unlikely that it seems like a miracle Compare: - a wonderful holiday - a miraculous escape Do not call an ordinary pleasant experience “miraculous” unless deliberately exaggerating.

falseSynonyms.zh: These look related but have very different modern meanings. - terrific = excellent - terrifying = frightening Example: - a terrific performance - a terrifying accident
falseSynonyms.point: These look related but have very different modern meanings. - terrific = excellent - terrifying = frightening Example: - a terrific performance - a terrifying accident

falseSynonyms.zh: Both can mean visually noticeable. - striking = noticeable, distinctive - stunning = extremely beautiful or impressive Example: - a striking contrast - a stunning view Useful in academic, professional, or restrained writing: - remarkable - extraordinary - exceptional - impressive - striking - astonishing - astounding Example: The study produced remarkable results. Useful in general speech and writing: - incredible - unbelievable - phenomenal - spectacular - stunning - breathtaking Useful for people, experiences, ideas, food, work, and events: - wonderful - marvellous / marvelous - fantastic - fabulous - terrific - awesome - mind-blowing These may be unsuitable for very formal academic writing. - miraculous — extraordinarily unlikely, like a miracle - awe-inspiring — produces awe - breathtaking — beauty/drama that figuratively takes your breath away - spectacular — visually dramatic - striking — immediately noticeable
falseSynonyms.point: Both can mean visually noticeable. - striking = noticeable, distinctive - stunning = extremely beautiful or impressive Example: - a striking contrast - a stunning view Useful in academic, professional, or restrained writing: - remarkable - extraordinary - exceptional - impressive - striking - astonishing - astounding Example: The study produced remarkable results. Useful in general speech and writing: - incredible - unbelievable - phenomenal - spectacular - stunning - breathtaking Useful for people, experiences, ideas, food, work, and events: - wonderful - marvellous / marvelous - fantastic - fabulous - terrific - awesome - mind-blowing These may be unsuitable for very formal academic writing. - miraculous — extraordinarily unlikely, like a miracle - awe-inspiring — produces awe - breathtaking — beauty/drama that figuratively takes your breath away - spectacular — visually dramatic - striking — immediately noticeable
